content.comment_body: I just started using [product_name] and tried to add two normally open contacts in parallel with an output to create an OR logic, but the software didn't allow it. I read that this action is not permitted. How can I implement an OR circuit?
Which programming language do you use—Ladder diagram (LAD) or Function Block Diagram (FBD)?
You can create an OR logic in both LAD and FBD.
Thanks for your help. I was working with ladder diagrams and tried the configuration shown in the image, but the program wouldn't accept it, which is why I asked. It might be better to use FBD.
I've attached a screen video showing how to create an OR function in LAD.

There are basic rules for using LAD. The output of a contact should only connect to the next input or to a coil within the network. Avoid connecting two outputs together, as this will result in a fault. If you have trouble inserting contacts, try deleting lines first, then place the new contacts and recreate the connections as described. Regards, [user_name]
FBD is generally the better choice. LAD in [product_name] is prone to bugs and offers fewer features compared to FBD.
Thank you, I'll try that. I'll also keep in mind the advice that LAD has issues in [product_name], and that FBD is preferable. Thanks everyone!

LAD resembles wiring diagrams and is beneficial for electricians. If you're aware of the bugs, LAD isn't too bad for creating clean programs. Recent updates have reduced some issues, but not all are resolved. I prefer LAD at [company_name] because the programs are easier to follow without cross references. In FBD, you need more lines or cross references for each signal. I've used FBD with UDF blocks to minimize cross references. After comparing LAD and FBD on the same task, LAD required 30% fewer blocks. The challenge is that all functions must be completed within a UDF, often needing extra status information and blocks. Maybe in future versions, FBD signals can be reused as needed, so I might try making clearer programs with FBD again. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience challenges when building OR logic in ladder diagrams (LAD) within [product_name] software, as the platform restricts adding normally open contacts in parallel for OR operations. Feedback highlights that Function Block Diagram (FBD) supports these functions better and is less prone to bugs than LAD. Overall, reliability and usability concerns with LAD—especially around contact placement—reduce confidence in using this mode.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to use ladder diagrams in [product_name] to easily add parallel contacts for OR logic operations, without encountering restrictions or software bugs.
